div.head: III Atr Prol.
div.ab: Ðis syndon þa lága, þe Æðelred cyng ⁊ his witan gerædd habbað æt Wánetingc to friðes bóte.
Hę sunt leges, quas Æþelredus rex et sapientes sui constituerunt apud Wanetingum ad emendationem pacis et felicitatis incrementum.
Ðis syndon þa lága þe Æðelred cyng ⁊ his witan gerædd habbað æt Wánetingc to friðes bóte.
Dies sind die Gesetze, welche König Aethelred und seine Witan beschlossen haben zu Wantage, zur Besserung öffentlicher Sicherheit.
Prologue. These are the laws which King Æthelred and his witan have decided at Wantage, for the improvement of public security.
These are the constitutions which King Æthelred and his councillors have enacted at Wantage for the promotion of public security.
These are the laws which King Ethelred and his councillors have decreed at Wantage, for the improvement of public security.

div.note: The Latin is the Quadripartitus (after I Atr in the Quadr. MSS). Liebermann's Old English base text H (Textus Roffensis f. 48, after ‘Willelmes asetnysse’, c. 1125). Dated 981–1012 (997?). ‘æfter Dena lage’ may have followed in the original (Liebermann; compare I Atr Prol.). Quadr.'s ‘et felicitatis incrementum’ is its own addition.; F: corrected against Liebermann, Gesetze I (date in the running heads), October 2026 (was “981–1012 or ?997; probably 997 (Whitelock); ?mid–990's (Wormald); Wantage, Wessex”, now “981–1012 or ?997 (Liebermann); probably 997 (Whitelock); ?mid–990's (Wormald); Wantage, Wessex”)

note.seg: Die Form des Prologs gleicht der zu I Atr
The form of the prologue resembles that of I Atr
Es steht statt des dortigen Englischen Wortes hier Nordisches Lehnwort laga
Here, instead of the English word used there, the Norse loan-word laga appears
S. o. Einl. 2
See above Introduction 2

Die Hinzufügung in Q scheint, laut Sinnes und des ihm lieben Wortschatzes, dessen Eigentum.—Für die von mir vermutete Ergänzung ‘nach Denalagu’ spricht der Inhalt von III Atr und die Parallele zu I Atr Pro ‘nach Engländer Recht’

The addition in Q appears, to judge from the sense and from the vocabulary he favours, to be his own.—The supplement ‘according to the Danelaw’ that I have conjectured is supported by the content of III Atr and by the parallel in I Atr Pro ‘according to English law’
Cf. IV Edg. 2, 1 and note.

Wantage in Berkshire, a royal manor (see DB. i. 57 a), was the birthplace of Alfred (see Asser, Life of K. Alfred, ed. Stevenson, p. 1). An assembly was held there in 997 (see Kemble, 698) and another is recorded (Kemble, 693) æt Cwicelmes-hlæwe, i.e. probably Cuckhamsley Hill in the vicinity of Wantage.
Q adds et felicitatis incrementum.
